title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is typescript page '- 34 -'. It is a stray leaf: a Bourbaki-style expository draft on analytic functions of several variables, filed among Grothendieck's handwritten 1965 notes on A-linear categories and motifs. Its content has nothing to do with the neighbouring pages.

Setting: K is R or C, A and B are domains (connected open sets) in K^p, and E is presumably a complete normed (or Banach) space.

(1) End of a gluing statement. If f is holomorphic on A, g on B, A∩B is connected and f=g on A∩B, then the function equal to f on A and to g on B is holomorphic on A∪B. This is the analytic continuation of f (or of g) to A∪B.

(2) Proposition 1. Take a family of domains (A_α) whose pairwise intersections are empty or connected, and holomorphic E-valued f_α on A_α. Suppose f_α and f_β agree on some nonempty open subset of each nonempty A_α∩A_β. Then there is a unique holomorphic f on ∪A_α restricting to each f_α. Proof: the identity theorem ('th.1') applied on the connected set A_α∩A_β gives f_α=f_β on the whole intersection, so the f_α glue.

(3) §2, 'Maximal domains of existence; singular points'. Consider the set M of holomorphic extensions of f to domains containing A, ordered by restriction. M is inductive: the union of a chain of domains containing A is a domain, and the functions glue. By Zorn's lemma there is a maximal extension f_0 on a domain A_0, a 'maximal domain of existence' for f. On a given maximal A_0 the maximal extension is unique, by the identity theorem. If A_0=K^p it is the only maximal domain. The page then breaks off. Implicitly, maximal schlicht domains are not unique in general (e.g. the logarithm), which is why the text says 'un' and not 'le' domaine maximal.

This is standard background for the elementary theory of analytic continuation in K^p without Riemann domains / étalé spaces; singular points are presumably defined next.
errors: No mathematical errors. Hypotheses implicit on this page: K must be R or C (or connectedness arguments must otherwise make sense), and th.1 is the identity theorem on connected open sets. The Zorn argument tacitly needs that a union of a chain of domains containing A is connected, and that M is a set; both are immediate.
Typographical issues only: 'telsque', 'ma-ximaux', 'aussitôt' cut off at the margin.

ideas.what: Gluing holomorphic functions on domains with connected pairwise intersections via the identity theorem
ideas.modern_name: Analytic continuation / sheaf property of holomorphic functions plus the identity theorem
ideas.where_published: Standard texts (e.g. Bourbaki, Variétés différentielles et analytiques, fascicule de résultats; Dieudonné, Foundations of Modern Analysis)

ideas.what: Existence of a maximal analytic continuation inside K^p via Zorn's lemma; uniqueness of the extension on a given maximal domain
ideas.modern_name: Maximal (schlicht) domain of existence / domain of holomorphy of a germ
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Weierstrass for C; Cartan–Thullen for several variables)
